story.title: The story behind the release
story.description:
We got Maylo as an adult dog. He originally came from Poland, had already been adopted once in Germany, and was returned to the shelter because he bit. He would snap if a hand approached too quickly. But this was simply because he thought he was being hit. With a lot of patience and calm, we were able to overcome his fear. Within a very short time, he completely changed his behavior, regained his trust, and became an absolute model student.

There was also a serious dog bite incident at the shelter where he was almost killed by a Doberman. The animal welfare organization invested a lot of money to save him. Consequently, he was initially afraid of large dogs in particular. After many positive encounters, this fear completely disappeared.

He was only with us for 2.5 years before the cancer diagnosis, but in that time, he etched himself into our hearts forever. It started with a slight limp, which later turned out to be bone marrow cancer. It wasn't even two months before we had to let him go. These songs describe the emotional journey we went through during this difficult time.

about.title: About this album
about.description: Born in Magdeburg on October 31, 1935 — a twin, the son of a fishmonger — Horst Schnell grew up under the bombs of World War II, came of age under a regime he refused to serve, and escaped East Germany in March 1958 carrying little more than a rucksack. He found his footing in the Rhineland, met Annemarie at a Pentecost dance in the Neandertal valley, built a career from scratch, earned a doctorate, and held a worldwide patent for an oil-air lubrication system. Through losses that would have broken most people and joys that sustained him, one belief never wavered: peace is the highest good. These 20 songs were written by his son Oliver for his 90th birthday — a portrait, not a summary.

about.title: About
about.description: Horst Schnell was born on October 31, 1935, in Magdeburg — a twin, the son of Emmy and Paul, who ran a fish shop at the Hasselbach Platz. He was nine years old when British bombers turned Magdeburg into a sea of fire on the night of February 7, 1945. The family fled, returned to rubble, and spent the postwar years trading fish tins for potatoes. Growing up in the Soviet occupation zone, Horst refused to join the Free German Youth — a quiet act of resistance that required real courage. He watched Russian tanks roll through the streets on June 17, 1953. In March 1958, at the age of 22, he crossed into West Berlin with a rucksack, a borrowed FDJ shirt, and no plan beyond escape. In Duisburg he came close to dying — Tetanie, bronchial asthma, heartbreak, and exhaustion left him nearly without hope. His brother Paul drove from Wuppertal and brought him back. A kind landlady in Mettmann gave him a room and a sense of home. At a Pentecost dance in the Schwarzwaldhaus in the Neandertal valley in 1960, he met Annemarie Ruhrberg. They married on September 8, 1961. Working as an engineer by day and studying by correspondence in the evenings, he earned a Diplom-Ingenieur and eventually his doctorate — his dissertation on fractal geometry. He invented an oil-air lubrication system, had it patented in Europe, Canada, and America, and received an environmental award. Then, on July 4, 1975, his daughter Dagmar died in his arms following a car accident. He and Annemarie adopted a foster daughter, Kirstin, fulfilling Dagmar's last wish. Son Oliver was born on March 29, 1978, and daughter Angela on February 1, 1983. Through war, escape, illness, professional triumph, and the deepest personal loss, one conviction held steady: Der Friede ist das höchste Gut. Peace is the highest good.
about.albumDescription: "Lieder eines Lebens" — Songs of a Life — was composed by Oliver Schnell for his father's 90th birthday. Each of the 20 tracks is drawn from a real chapter in Horst Schnell's life: the firebombing of Magdeburg, the years under Soviet rule, the escape to the West, the long climb from illness to engineering doctorate, a chance encounter at a dance in the Neandertal valley that became a marriage, a daughter lost on a summer's day, and the steady faith that peace — between people, between generations — is the highest thing we can reach for. The album does not idealize or summarize. It bears witness.
